To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD11b inactivating NIF(+/+)/CD11b(+/+) mice are protected against E. coli sepsis induced ALI.

inactivation of CD11beta in a mouse transgene model protects against septicemia-induced lung neutrophil infiltration and vascular injury by interfering with neutrophil adhesion to the vascular endothelium.

CD11b inactivating NIF(+/) mice were protected from E. coli sepsis-induced PMN lung infiltration and vascular injury, and that the NIF(+) transgenic mouse is a potentially useful animal model for in vivo studies of the role of CD11b on PMNs in the mechanisms of vascular inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PMNs and their integrin CD11b in acute inflammation, with a particular focus on the mechanisms of lung vascular injury induced by PMNs in sepsis.
the role of CD11b/CD18 (Mac-1) on the adhesion of PMN to vascular endothelial cells and the role of this adhesion in the pathophysiology of acute lung injury.
the role of CD11b on PMN adhesion to vascular endothelium and the role of PMNs in the development of vascular injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD11b blockade in the early phase after E. coli injection prevents lung PMN accumulation and lung vascular injury, and this is associated with a significant reduction in lung edema formation.
CD11b inactivating polypeptide NIF is effective in blocking CD11b-dependent PMN function in vitro and PMN sequestrations in vivo.

the CD11b inactivated mice are resistant to the early lung PMN sequestation and vascular permeability increase induced by gram-negative septicemic shock, and this resistance is associated with the blockade of PMN CD 11b.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD11b is a crucial adhesion molecule for neutrophil recruitment and vascular permeability in the lung in response to gram-negative septic shock.
CD11b inactivaton in NIF(+) transgenic mice protects mice against E. coli sepsis-induced ALI by reducing lung PMN infiltration.
CD11b blockade in NIF(+) mice protects against lung PMN infiltration, vascular injury, and lung edema formation during the early phase of E. coli septicemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD11b blockade in vivo can protect from lung vascular injury in sepsis.

the CD11b integrin is a crucial mediator of PMN infiltration into the lung during the early phase of sepsis and that inactivation of the CD11b by the NIF polypeptide can prevent PMN-mediated lung injury in the early stages of sepsis.
CD11b blockade is a promising approach for treating ALI.
